title: refactor(types)!: retire `ObjectKanbanSchema.allowCollapse` on both faces (#8801)
body:
Fixes #8801

Retires `ObjectKanbanSchema.allowCollapse` on the `object-kanban` arm, on both
published faces, under ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove. Executes the director seat's
class-1 self-adjudication of 2026-09-16 (letter A — retire; B, wiring a reader,
was refused as a capability nobody asked for).

## What the key was

Declared on the TypeScript face (`allowCollapse?: boolean`) and on the zod
mirror (`z.boolean().optional()`), and read by **no registered board**. An
author who wrote `allowCollapse: true` type-checked green, parsed green, and got
a board that never collapsed anything off it — a published entry point with
nothing behind it.

## What landed

| face | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` | `allowCollapse?: boolean` | `allowCollapse?: never` (tombstone) |
| `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` | `z.boolean().optional().describe(...)` | `retirementTombstone(...)` |

An **ADR-0087 D2 tombstone, not a deletion**, and that is load-bearing:
`BaseSchema` carries an index signature and its mirror ends `.passthrough()`, so
a dropped member would be **kept, not refused** — one silent no-op traded for
another. The member stays declared and unwritable, so the value is refused BY
NAME with a prescription attached.

## Premises, re-measured on this branch rather than inherited

Every one of the four the card rests on was re-taken here, each with a control
firing on the same instrument in the same run.

1. **Upstream does not declare it.** Re-taken against the **installed**
   `@objectstack/spec` (17.4.0) in this worktree, not the shared checkout.
   `ObjectKanbanPropsSchema` — `ComponentPropsMap['object-kanban']` — declares
   `objectName groupBy columns filter limit data cardTitle titleField cardFields
   swimlaneField grouping quickAdd coverImageField conditionalFormatting`, and
   no `allowCollapse`. Token counts over the published package:
   `allowCollapse` **0** in `src` / `dist` / `json-schema`; controls `groupBy`
   **12 / 52 / 37** and `coverImageField` **1 / 4 / 2**; a minted absent token
   scored **0 / 0 / 0**. ⚠️ One correction to the ruling's prose, which does not
   move the verdict: `groupField` appears in that schema as an **alias** entry
   (`groupField` to `groupBy`), not as a declared member. ⭐ And the schema is a
   `strictObject`, so the platform was **already** refusing an authored
   `allowCollapse` by name at publish while this face said yes.
2. **objectui declared it on both faces.** Re-derived by symbol, not by the line
   address the ruling quoted: one declaration inside `interface
   ObjectKanbanSchema` and one inside `export const ObjectKanbanSchema` on the
   mirror. CONFIRMED.
3. **No registered board reads it.** Zero files under `packages/plugin-kanban`
   name the token, against firing controls in the same pass — `groupBy` **45
   files**, `conditionalFormatting` **8**, `quickAdd` **6**, `coverImageField`
   **3** — and a freshly minted absent token at **0**. Repo-wide, no file under
   any `packages/*/src` names it at all.
4. **Batch #70's retirement did not reach here, and still does not.** What
   survives of it is an explanatory block on the `kanban` mirror recording that
   its refusals were arm-scoped by construction and that an `object-kanban`
   document "is judged exactly as it always was". The tombstone landed here
   agrees with that rather than contradicting it: this is a separate ruling on
   this arm's own protocol row.

### ⭐ The grep is not the reading — both unnamed channels were traced to their ends

A renderer can consume a key it never names, so a source grep alone cannot
answer the inertness question. Both channels terminate before any sink:

- **PROP channel.** `SchemaRenderer` spreads every non-metadata key as a React
  prop; `ObjectKanbanRenderer` destructures `schema` and forwards its rest into
  `ObjectKanban`, whose first statement after its own destructure is
  `void _props;`. The rest is discarded, never spread onward.
- **SCHEMA channel.** The key **does** ride `ObjectKanban`'s `{ ...schema }`
  spread into `effectiveSchema`, and reaches `KanbanRenderer` — which
  destructures `schema` / `objectFields` / `onCardMove` and **names every key**
  it hands to the lazy board. An unnamed key stops there.

Both terminators are pinned as source text in the new test, so the reading is
re-derived on every run rather than remembered.

## Evidence on the BUILT artifact

The BREAKING banner is earned on `dist` — the bytes a consumer installs — not on
`src`. `dist/objectql.d.ts` carries `allowCollapse?: never;` and
`dist/zod/objectql.zod.d.ts` carries an OPTIONAL of `z.ZodNever`; the previous
spelling survives nowhere under `dist`. Parsed through the built entry:

```
{ allowCollapse: true } | { allowCollapse: false } | { allowCollapse: 'yes' }
                                                  RED  invalid_type at `allowCollapse`
{ groupField: 'status' }                          RED  invalid_type at `groupField`   <- OTHER TOMBSTONE
{ quickAdd: true } · { coverImageField: 'cover' } · { limit: 50 }
                                                  GREEN                               <- LIVE CONTROLS
{ allowCollapsing: true }                         GREEN                               <- NEAR-MISS CONTROL
```

Live members parse green, so the arm is not refusing everything. ⭐ The near miss
parsing **green** is the discriminator that makes the tombstone load-bearing:
this arm is not strict, so a never-declared neighbour is kept rather than
refused — which is exactly what deleting the member would have shipped.

## Pins, in both directions

New: `packages/types/src/__tests__/object-kanban-allow-collapse-retired-8801.test.ts`.

- **Refused by name** — an issue at the key's OWN path, code `invalid_type`, for
  `true` / `false` / a string alike; the message asserted for the ruling's own
  required content (that lane collapse is `KanbanColumn.collapsed`'s and **not a
  board-level authored toggle**), not frozen as a whole paragraph.
- **The declared members still parse** — nine live members each accepted, plus
  the bare node as the firing control, plus this arm's OTHER tombstone
  (`groupField`) still refusing, so the narrowing did not sweep the arm.
- **One string, both channels** — the `.describe()` metadata is asserted to be
  the parse message, the invariant `retirementTombstone()` exists for.
- **Type-level** — the member evaluates to exactly `undefined` and is not `any`
  (deleting it instead would fall through the index signature to `any`, and
  that pin would go red), with a live member as the non-vacuity control and an
  unused-directive `@ts-expect-error` literal that goes red with TS2578 if the
  tombstone is ever widened back.
- **Tree-scoped absence** — no property read of the key anywhere under
  `packages/` or `apps/`, with a firing control in the same walk. Tree-scoped on
  purpose: a file-scoped pin sees only the files its author thought of.

Moved, not deleted: `bare-kanban-node-key-retired-8802.test.ts` suite 3 asserted
that this arm still **accepted** the key. That row is now a refusal assertion
with its reason stated at the site; its three sibling rows stay accepting,
because the claim that suite makes — batch #70's refusals were arm-scoped and
cannot cross an arm — is still true, and this retirement is not that claim.

## Region fence

The claim released this lane at **region** granularity, not file granularity:
`packages/types/src/objectql.ts` and `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`
are both held by open PR #9540, frozen head, whose region is
`ObjectGallerySchema.filter`. **The fence held.** Both hunks fall inside the
`ObjectKanbanSchema` region of their file and carry that symbol as their hunk
context header; `ObjectGallerySchema` sits several hundred lines further down in
the declaration file and is untouched, as is that PR and its branch. Nothing
here required stepping outside the region.

## Gates

Hand-derived from this repo's own `check:*` scripts and workflows —
`dispatch-gates.mjs` refuses cross-repo and cannot answer for this repository,
so `--ran` reconciliation is unavailable here and is stated as such rather than
faked. Exit codes captured to disk as each ran, before any pipe.

## Acceptance notes

- **Owed follow-up, deliberately not taken here.** `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`
  carries a note that reads, in part, that `@object-ui/types` "still declares
  both on its mirror of this face, so a reader will find them there; that half
  is objectui#8801, not this table." This pull request lands that half, so the
  sentence is now stale. The file is **outside the file surface this lane was
  released on**, and the claim's instruction on a breach is to stop and report
  rather than widen — so it is reported instead of edited. It is a prose
  staleness, not a gate failure: no gate reads it, and the note fails loudly
  rather than silently for anyone who acts on it (the key is now refused by
  name). Dedupe words: schema-reference, allowCollapse, object-kanban, mirror,
  stale.
- **Recorded, not filed.** The doc note's sibling subject `quickAdd` — retired
  by objectui#8285 on the strict authoring face while this mirror still declares
  it live — is the other half of that same paragraph and is **not** this card.
  No action taken, named here only so the next reader of that note knows which
  half moved.
